problem: Existing VLM-based VLN-CE policies map observations directly to actions with no explicit supervision on world state, action-induced transitions or future states. World-model navigation methods treat policy, dynamics and future generation as separate or partial components and often keep the world model running at inference, which adds compute.
motivation: Good navigation needs an understanding of how the world state changes under the agent's actions, which pure action imitation does not teach. Auxiliary world-modeling objectives applied only during training could give richer supervision at no inference cost.
key_idea: Train a single VLM navigation policy, with frozen VGGT spatial features fused into its visual tokens, jointly with action, inverse-dynamics, forward-dynamics and future-generation objectives, and use only the action policy at inference.
insight: The auxiliary objectives give complementary supervision beyond action imitation. Forward dynamics helps most on its own (SR 50.1→53.0), and combining all three reaches 55.1 SR (component ablation, 0K setting). The prediction target matters: spatial (VGGT) latents (55.1 SR) beat DINO (51.8), VLM visual (51.4) and VAE (51.0) latents. World-action training also speeds convergence: the policy-only baseline's final SR of 50.2 is matched after about 63% of the schedule.
method: Backbone: Qwen3-VL-4B/8B autoregressive policy decodes text actions STOP/MOVE_FORWARD/TURN_LEFT/TURN_RIGHT from the instruction and RGB history, trained with next-token CE.

Spatial encoder + merger: a frozen VGGT gives intermediate-layer spatial tokens (2048-d); RMSNorm and a 2-layer MLP merger project them to the LLM hidden size, and they are added to the VLM visual tokens as E^v = E^q + αE^g with α=0.2.
Forward dynamics head: an MLP on [last image-token hidden state; teacher-forced GT action-token hidden state] regresses the pooled next-frame spatial feature (MSE).
Inverse dynamics head: classifies the executed action from [context hidden; previous pooled visual hidden; current pooled visual hidden; their difference] (CE).
Future generation head: an action-free MLP on [context hidden; current pooled visual hidden] predicts the next spatial feature (MSE).

Training objective: L = L_policy + 0.1(L_forward + L_inverse + L_gen); the LLM, merger and heads are optimized while the vision tower and VGGT stay frozen. Inference uses only the policy branch, so there is no extra cost.

setting.training_data: 0K setting: R2R-CE and RxR-CE expert trajectories only (~2.43M samples: 631K R2R, 1.80M RxR). Full setting adds ScaleVLN and DAgger rollouts (~10.4M external samples).
setting.observation: monocular RGB history (single RGB camera, no depth/odometry/panorama)

numbers.extra: only R2R/RxR-CE expert trajectories, no external data

numbers_note: Real-world results are qualitative only. The ablation tables (component and latent) use the 4B 0K setting.
results: FutureNav-4B with external data reaches 65.4 SR / 61.3 SPL on R2R-CE val-unseen, beating JanusVLN (60.5/56.8). FutureNav-8B reaches 63.9 SR / 54.8 SPL on RxR-CE, beating JanusVLN and NavFoM (57.4 SR). With only VLN-CE expert data, FutureNav-4B† gets 55.1 SR vs JanusVLN† 52.8.
limitations: Only R2R-CE and RxR-CE in simulation are evaluated; the real-world zero-shot results are qualitative, with no quantitative metrics.
The dynamics and future heads are unused at inference, so the model gets no look-ahead planning benefit.
Comparisons with the strongest baselines involve differing external data budgets, and the largest gains rely on ~10M external samples.
